findings.description: F001 says the listed guarded commands are the complete plan-mutating surface, but F002 and F003 also add plan worktree create/remove behavior under the plan namespace. The contract separates guard, cleanup, and create rules, so the plan should explicitly classify those subcommands instead of relying on a contradictory completeness claim.
findings.recommendation: Clarify that F001 owns only the named non-worktree plan-mutating guard surface, and separately state the enforcement model for plan worktree create/remove.

findings.description: F002 requires gitignored content to block removal and be reported, but the enumerated tests do not pin an ignored-content refusal fixture. This is central to the preservation outcome and could regress while still satisfying the listed dirty and untracked tests.
findings.recommendation: Add a fixture with a gitignored file under the worktree and assert refusal, explicit ignored-path output, no audit entry claiming removal, no registry deletion, and worktree untouched.

findings.description: F003 pins missing-config notices by default and divergent refusal during opt-in copy, but it does not clearly require default create-time detection and reporting of an already-present divergent allowlisted file. The objective says missing and divergent operator-local config must be declared explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Specify the no-copy path for divergent allowlisted files: detect, report, and refuse or otherwise explicitly define the expected outcome, then test it.

findings.description: The completion test requires fixture tests with zero live auditor calls, but F001 does not explicitly pin auditor stubbing or no-network assertions for audit and orchestrate dispatch entry-point tests. Those commands are the most likely to accidentally cross into live auditor behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add a test-matrix rule that all guard tests use fixture-only auditor/orchestrator adapters and assert no live auditor or network path is invoked.
